experiment_data.hypothesis: Bootstrap empirical null of lz* under 4PL model shows systematic positive bias (mean>>0) and inflated variance (std>>1) for real LLM response data, quantifying the degree to which LLMs violate IRT local independence/unidimensionality assumptions — this bias explains why 95% of cells are flagged with absolute thresholds

spec.eval_data: combine.csv 12×41871 binary responses, 5 benchmark param sets

metrics.key_finding: Null bias is small (mean=0.09) and std is near 1.0 — the bootstrap null is well-calibrated. The 95% flagging rate is NOT caused by miscalibrated null but by genuine extreme lz* values in LLM data. Smaller benchmarks (humaneval, arc_c) show higher KS rejection rates due to stronger finite-sample deviations from normality.
